name: Relationship-matched navigation mechanisms
summary: Choose navigation representation according to site scope, local section, hierarchical ancestry, related peer destination, or linear task-flow relation.
problem: Breadcrumbs, sidebars, menus, back links and tabs are treated as interchangeable by visual preference rather than information relationship.
context: Multi-region products combining site/service navigation, detail hierarchy, related views and sequential tasks.
observed_solution: Map global navigation to major site areas, local nav to section children, breadcrumbs to ancestors, task lists/back links to linear journeys, and links to related destinations; name separate nav regions.
rationale: GOV site/service/journey distinctions O16/O17/O19/O20; USWDS header/local rail/breadcrumb scopes O24/O26/O28; WAI nav labels O14; Primer NavList/breadcrumb/UnderlineNav O31/O32/O33.
tradeoffs: Different mechanisms increase choice and can duplicate links.
Task language and hierarchy require product-specific user research.
applicability: Products with multiple distinct navigation relationships and enough complexity to merit more than one mechanism.
non_applicability: Flat websites with one simple header.
Interfaces whose visible controls are application commands, not destinations.
accessibility_implications: Label multiple nav landmarks; preserve link purpose and clear current context.
performance_implications: No evidence of performance outcomes from adding/removing nav mechanisms.
responsive_implications: Preserve important destinations under W04-P01/A01; avoid over-reducing hierarchy.
implementation_notes: USWDS 1–3 side levels are only local system convention.
Avoid organization-chart-as-IA claims absent user testing.
No universal sitemap or depth maximum.

counterexamples.summary: A simple public-service transaction can avoid broad service navigation in favor of a linear task structure.

version_context: WCAG 2.2, live GOV.UK/USWDS/Primer/WAI documentation; no project IA testing
accepted_by: KIRION Forge Maintainer under Kirch Technical Authority
